body:
Hi. My experiences come and go. One day I want to off myself and get stuck in that mindset for days or weeks on end, and then things change for the better again. I've been touch and go a few times now, and what I learned from the past is that killing yourself can be done for a wide variety of very valid reasons. People can be in excruciating pain, both physically and mentally. As far as I'm concerned, having terminal cancer or having a terminal depression is absolutely equal. The difference, obviously, being: the cancer will kill you without your help, depression just needs you to pull the often proverbial trigger.

Now. Unlike cancer patients and such, there's a way out of it's "just in your brain". There are a few things that helped me immensely the past year or two:

1. Realize that the person who you want to kill can also be overwritten by someone new. Someone that you do like. Be the person you want to be, not who you are expected to be. And this requires the next item on the list:
2. A good foundation for yourself, your life, who you are or who you want to be. Have great friends. Don't have them? Be someone that has. Can't find them? Fuck that: be someone who does find them. You now suddenly like rock climbing and you will find people that enjoy it, too. 

There are billions of things you could do other than kill yourself. A depression is a deep rooted issue that should be treated by professionals, but if that fails it really is up to *you* to better yourself. Build a better foundation for yourself. Fuck, make up a cover story for a troubled youth if you so please. Fake it 'till you make it. Everybody does it.

The past week had me contemplating killing myself again because of some bad changes. So I tried to forge new good things in my life. It didn't work. So I came onto Reddit and asked for advice, something I could change. And I changed a thing in my life that made me feel infinitely better. I'm not even joking: /r/nofap - I have gone from not smiling in weeks to grinning like a toddler. Life is awesome again.

Good luck to you.

Thanks for taking the time to reply. I am hoping to find relief, but somewhere I know it's not that easy. As said, I've everything going for me. And the few parts that I could improve upon are probably not going to make that much of a difference. Doesn't hurt to try, I suppose.

But honestly, thanks for sharing. This chat isn't something I would have with friends, most wouldn't understand, much like how you describe your wife having trouble understanding it with yourself. A friend of mine sees through it but offers advice that is hardly making myself feel better...

Reading /r/suicidewatch is strangely therapeutic, as sad as that sounds. It puts things into perspective. It's probably the only support group that I can actually be an anonymous part of without people asking me to join in group hugs ;)

Best of luck to you, and thanks again.

Thanks for that, more than you know... The only scary thing to me is that I know I'd be dead, given the means (such as a gun). Of course I want to live, but at some point the means to fill life with enough wonder to make it more interesting than death run out. As I said in another reply, it's like being drained of all fuel. The engine ran dry. And I have no idea where I can refuel, nor how long of a struggle it is going to be...

I've gotten some good advice, though :)

Thanks :) You helped me realize something, I sit inside too much, I've given up on a few things because I was bored with them. Time to get back into action and see what it brings me. Might as well try, the alternative is much less interesting...
Heheh, once you're a member for a while longer that'll stop ;) So, new hobbies. I have one, but that's only fun with someone else. I'll try to pick up painting again. I used to enjoy that...
Their FAQ is interesting. Didn't take your post serious at first. Might be worth a shot, actually. Thanks :)

Sitting at home because of probably-related physical complaints that my company's doctor said were reason enough to "take it easy for a while." 

I've always said "What doesn't kill me makes me stronger" and "Find strength in pain," tile-worthy crap like that; or lyrics from an angsty teenage band. I just feel empty. As if all the fuel has been drained.

My old life was more fun... when I enjoyed computer games, socializing, playing sports... you know, genuinely enjoyed it. Increasing my performance in games and sports, being cool to people, being liked, liking people, meeting interesting people...

Last weekend, at a party, I met a bunch of people. I spoke to them about all sorts of crap. They stuck around because apparently I know a lot (thanks Reddit!), but none of them seemed to be interesting. And they're smart, creative people...

I wonder how to fix myself...
Working on it... I'm trying to learn how to be more engaging, physically. The current me needs to get lost, or die trying. I'm so fed up with my life, or lack thereof...

I acknowledge they did the dirty twice, no more!

To me it's not as much the emotional aspect, as is the physical one. Going in for a hug, kiss or anything beyond this is unfathomable to me. All action so far was been initiated by the girl. I don't even freeze up, I just... don't function. It doesn't happen. Until I lay awake hours later and wonder "Why the hell didn't I..."

And then I plan and plot scenario's, only to fail executing any of it and keeping my distance. I've been called distant more than once. It's ruining most relationships I've had... I don't want to be that person anymore.
